newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber dull on Japan, Thailand holidays.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber dull on Japan, Thailand holidays.

text.p: The Singapore rubber market was quiet by midday on Monday with holidays in Japan and Thailand keeping most of the trade on the sidelines, dealers said.

Market players were just trickling back into their offices after leaving last Wednesday to celebrate the May Day holiday and skipping Friday to attend the annual industry dinner in the Thai rubber centre of Hat Yai last Friday.
"Very few people are back. The long stretch of holidays affected trading this morning," a trader said.
News of the end of the nearly three week-long strike in Goodyear Tire was greeted cautiously by dealers.
"I think the workers still have to ratify the agreement so we have to see how that situation works out," a trader said.
Dealers said the market was looking for leads in the afternoon session. "Most of the big boys are out so we're looking for any kind of a lift," a dealer said.
The Thai government's decision to increase its support price for RSS3 grade rubber was ignored by the market, dealers said.
At 0430 GMT, June RSS3 was indicated unchanged at 107.50 U.S. cents a kg. June RSS1 was indicated at 156.00 Singapore cents (US$1.08) a kg from 155.50 cents.
